items.claim: `Column.overflow` defaults to `"ellipsis"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Column dataclass declares `overflow: "OverflowMethod" = "ellipsis"`.

items.claim: In `Text.render`, the combined active styles are cached by the tuple of style ids.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: The cache key is a tuple of resolved `Style` objects (`styles = tuple(style_map[_style_id] ...)`), not a tuple of style ids.

items.claim: When a line is shorter than the crop width and `pad=False`, `adjust_line_length` copies the line unchanged without padding it out to the console width.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `adjust_line_length` lives in rich/segment.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: `ReprHighlighter` has four highlight patterns: tags, `name=value` pairs, braces, and one combined alternation.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `ReprHighlighter` is defined in rich/highlighter.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: `Console.push_render_hook(hook)` registers a `RenderHook` that receives renderables before output.
items.label: supported
items.reason: push_render_hook appends a RenderHook to the stack, and print calls hook.process_renderables on the renderables before rendering.

items.claim: `Text.split` takes an early return and returns `Lines` built from a copy when there are no newlines.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `split` defaults to separator "\n" and returns `Lines([self.copy()])` immediately if the separator is absent.

items.claim: The `Table` `show_edge` parameter defaults to `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Table.__init__ signature has `show_edge: bool = True`.

items.claim: In `Table._render`, body rows get their style from `get_row_style`, which composes alternating `row_styles` with any per-row style.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Non-header/footer rows use `get_row_style`, which alternates `row_styles[index % len(...)]` and adds the per-row style.

items.claim: `Console.save_text()` writes exported text directly to a file and is a wrapper around `export_text()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: save_text calls export_text and writes the result to the given path.

items.claim: The Console's buffer depth counter means nested prints only increment it and nothing reaches the file until the outermost context exits.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_enter_buffer`/`_exit_buffer` adjust `_buffer_index`, and `_write_buffer` only writes and clears when `_buffer_index == 0`.

items.claim: `Padding.unpack` raises `ValueError` naming the length it received for any other number of values.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The final line raises `ValueError(f"1, 2 or 4 integers required for padding; {len(pad)} given")`.

items.claim: `Console.width` returns `self._width` in preference to any OS-reported width.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `width` returns `size.width`, which uses `self._width` whenever it is not None, ignoring `os.get_terminal_size`.

items.claim: `Style` instances can be combined with the `+` operator via `__add__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Style defines __add__ which combines styles via _add.

items.claim: In `Console.get_style`, a `StyleSyntaxError` from `Style.parse` is converted to `errors.MissingStyle` and propagates out of `print`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `get_style` catches `StyleSyntaxError` and raises `errors.MissingStyle`, and `print` calls `get_style(style)` unguarded so the error propagates.

items.claim: `_write_buffer` resolves `self.file` twice, once for `write` and once for `flush`, and then runs `del self._buffer[:]`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The non-Windows branch does `self.file.write(text)` then `self.file.flush()` followed by `del self._buffer[:]`, each access re-resolving the `file` property.

items.claim: `cell_len` routes strings under 512 characters through an LRU cache of 4096 entries.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `cell_len` is implemented in rich/cells.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: `adjust_line_length` returns the line as a shallow copy unchanged when it is shorter than the target length and `pad=False`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `adjust_line_length` is defined in rich/segment.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: If the user presses Enter without typing and a default is set, that default is returned immediately without calling `process_response()`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: rich/prompt.py is not shown, so the default/Enter handling cannot be checked.

items.claim: `Color` is a NamedTuple with fields `name`, `type`, `number`, and `triplet`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Color is a NamedTuple with name, type, number and triplet fields.

items.claim: `_Cell` is a NamedTuple in rich/table.py with fields `style`, `renderable`, and `vertical`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _Cell is a NamedTuple with style, renderable and vertical fields.

items.claim: The pretty printing API detects recursive data structures using a set of object IDs to prevent infinite loops.
items.label: supported
items.reason: traverse keeps a visited_ids set of object ids and returns Node(value_repr="...") on recursion.

items.claim: `Style.parse()` supports links using the syntax "link URL".
items.label: supported
items.reason: Style.parse handles the word 'link' followed by a URL.

items.claim: `Padding.__rich_console__` renders its inner renderable at `width - left - right`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `render_options = options.update_width(width - self.left - self.right)` is used for the inner renderable.

items.claim: `Table.add_column` builds one `Column` dataclass and appends it to the table's columns.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `add_column` constructs a single `Column` dataclass and does `self.columns.append(column)`.

items.claim: `Console.export_text` reads from the record buffer.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `export_text` iterates `self._record_buffer` under the record buffer lock.

items.claim: `JupyterMixin` enables Rich objects to be rendered in Jupyter notebooks using the `_repr_mimebundle_` protocol.
items.label: supported
items.reason: JupyterMixin implements _repr_mimebundle_ returning text/plain and text/html.

items.claim: `ConsoleOptions.copy` builds a new instance with a shallow-copied `__dict__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `copy` uses `ConsoleOptions.__new__` and assigns `self.__dict__.copy()`.

items.claim: `Text.rstrip_end` does nothing when the text length is below the given width.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The body only executes when `text_length > size`, so nothing happens for shorter text.

items.claim: Measurement forces highlighting off.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Measurement.get` calls `console.render_str(renderable, markup=options.markup, highlight=False)`.

items.claim: The `Console` `safe_box` parameter restricts box characters to those renderable on legacy Windows.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The Console docstring documents safe_box as restricting box options that don't render on legacy Windows, and Table uses console.safe_box when substituting box characters.

items.claim: The GitHub Actions CI is triggered on every pull request.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: .github/workflows/pythonpackage.yml content is not shown, so trigger conditions cannot be verified.

items.claim: The `TTY_COMPATIBLE` environment variable set to `"1"` forces `is_terminal=True`, and `"0"` forces `is_terminal=False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: is_terminal returns False for TTY_COMPATIBLE == "0" and True for "1".

items.claim: `Constrain.__rich_measure__` calls `Measurement.get` after updating `options` with `self.width`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __rich_measure__ updates options width with self.width then calls Measurement.get.

items.claim: `Console.render` confirms the object has `__rich_console__` and is not itself a class before calling it.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `render` checks `hasattr(renderable, "__rich_console__") and not isinstance(renderable, type)` before invoking it.

items.claim: The `PromptBase` parameter `password` defaults to `False` and masks input characters.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: rich/prompt.py is not shown so PromptBase's password parameter cannot be checked.

items.claim: `Console.__exit__` calls `_exit_buffer`, which decrements `_buffer_index` and then calls `_check_buffer`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__exit__` calls `_exit_buffer`, which decrements `_buffer_index` then calls `_check_buffer`.

items.claim: The `TTY_INTERACTIVE` environment variable set to `"1"` forces `is_interactive=True`, and `"0"` forces `is_interactive=False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: TTY_INTERACTIVE of "0" sets force_interactive False and "1" sets it True, which determines is_interactive.

items.claim: The `ThemeStack` holds named styles such as `repr.number`, `table.header` and `log.time`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The Console only constructs ThemeStack(themes.DEFAULT); rich/theme.py and rich/default_styles.py (where style names like repr.number would be defined) are not shown, so the specific names cannot be checked.

items.claim: Rich deletes five control characters (`\r`, `\b`, `\a`, `\v`, `\f`) from every string it renders, with no flag to disable it.
items.label: supported
items.reason: STRIP_CONTROL_CODES lists exactly five codepoints (7, 8, 11, 12, 13 = \a, \b, \v, \f, \r) and Text.__init__ unconditionally applies strip_control_codes with no opt-out parameter.

items.claim: `Confirm` has `response_type = bool` and `choices = ["y", "n"]`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: rich/prompt.py containing Confirm is not shown.

items.claim: `Align.left()`, `Align.center()`, and `Align.right()` are class method shortcuts for the corresponding align values.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Align defines classmethods left, center and right that construct Align with the corresponding align value.

items.claim: `Task.total` is `Optional[float]`; a value of `None` triggers the pulse animation.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: rich/progress.py is not shown, so Task.total typing and pulse behaviour cannot be checked.

items.claim: `Table.add_row` appends a `Row` and distributes cell content to `Column._cells`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: add_row appends renderables to each Column._cells via add_cell and ends by appending a Row to self.rows.

items.claim: The `SegmentLines` class wraps an `Iterable[List[Segment]]` and implements `__rich_console__`, appending a newline segment after each row when `new_lines=True`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: SegmentLines is not defined in any shown file (rich/segment.py was not included), so the claim cannot be checked.

items.claim: `_ReadContext` is a ContextManager that calls `progress.start()` on enter and `progress.stop()` on exit.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _ReadContext subclasses ContextManager and calls self.progress.start() in __enter__ and self.progress.stop() in __exit__.

items.claim: A closing markup tag with nothing to close raises `MarkupError`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: An implicit closing tag with an empty style stack raises MarkupError("closing tag '[/]' ... has nothing to close").

items.claim: `Table.__init__` normalises `header_style` and `footer_style` with `or ""` so `None` becomes an empty string.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Table.__init__ sets self.header_style = header_style or "" and self.footer_style = footer_style or "".

items.claim: If `auto_refresh=True`, `Live.start()` creates and starts a `_RefreshThread`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Live.start creates a _RefreshThread and starts it when self.auto_refresh is true.

items.claim: `TimeElapsedColumn` renders elapsed time as `H:MM:SS`, shows `"-:--:--"` before the task starts, and uses `task.finished_time` when finished.
items.label: supported
items.reason: It uses task.finished_time when finished, returns '-:--:--' when elapsed is None (task not started), and formats via timedelta giving H:MM:SS.

items.claim: The first line of `ConsoleOptions.update` is `options = self.copy()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The body of ConsoleOptions.update begins with `options = self.copy()`.

items.claim: `Table.__rich_measure__` computes minimum width as the sum of each column's minimum measurement plus border overhead.
items.label: supported
items.reason: minimum_width is the sum of each column measurement's minimum plus _extra_width, which accounts for box edges/dividers.

items.claim: Pretty printing handles attrs objects using `attr.fields`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _get_attr_fields calls _attr_module.fields(type(obj)) and traverse uses it for attrs objects.

items.claim: `Table.__rich_console__` passes the content budget down with `options.update_width(...)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __rich_console__ computes column widths via self._calculate_column_widths(console, options.update_width(max_width - extra_width)).

items.claim: For a column with an explicit width, `Table._measure_column` does not inspect the cells.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When column.width is not None the method returns a fixed Measurement immediately, before iterating the column's cells.

items.claim: `ratio_distribute` from `rich/_ratio.py` distributes remaining space among flexible columns proportionally.
items.label: supported
items.reason: ratio_distribute is imported from ._ratio and called with the leftover flexible_width and the ratios of flexible columns to apportion space.

items.claim: `Table.add_section()` marks the most recently added row as the end of a section by setting `Row.end_section = True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: add_section sets self.rows[-1].end_section = True when rows exist.

items.claim: In `Inspect.__init__`, if `dunder=True` then `private` is also set to `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: self.private = private or dunder, so dunder=True forces private True.

items.claim: `ColorType.DEFAULT` has value 0 and represents the terminal default foreground/background.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: rich/color.py (where ColorType is defined) is not shown, so the enum value cannot be checked.

items.claim: `pick_bool` returns the first non-`None` of its arguments.
items.label: supported
items.reason: pick_bool loops over values and returns the first value that is not None (falling back to bool(value)).

items.claim: A zero-width joiner sequence counts as one cell under `cell_len`.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: In _cell_len a ZWJ merely causes the following character to be skipped, so the joined sequence takes the width of the leading character (2 cells for a wide emoji), not one cell.

items.claim: `Table.add_row` creates new unnamed columns automatically when more renderables are provided than columns exist.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When index == len(columns), a new Column is created, backfilled with blank cells, and appended.

items.claim: `Table.__init__` defaults `show_edge` to `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Table.__init__ declares show_edge: bool = True.

items.claim: `Span.extend(cells)` extends the span end by cells and returns a `Span`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Span.extend returns Span(start, end + cells, style) when cells is non-zero, else self.

items.claim: `JupyterMixin._repr_mimebundle_` returns a dict with both `text/plain` and `text/html` MIME types.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _repr_mimebundle_ builds data = {'text/plain': text, 'text/html': html}.

items.claim: `'bold'` is present in rich's style attribute table.
items.label: supported
items.reason: STYLE_ATTRIBUTES contains the key "bold" mapped to "bold".

items.claim: The `legacy_windows` flag chooses between the win32 API renderer and an ordinary `file.write` at the end of output.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _write_buffer checks self.legacy_windows (plus fileno) to decide between legacy_windows_render via LegacyWindowsTerm and plain self.file.write of the rendered text.

items.claim: rich/prompt.py provides `Prompt` and `Confirm` for interactive input.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both Prompt and Confirm classes are defined in rich/prompt.py for interactive input.

items.claim: In `Table._get_cells`, the header style is `get_style(self.header_style or "") + get_style(column.header_style)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The code is exactly header_style = get_style(self.header_style or "") + get_style(column.header_style).

items.claim: `Style.parse` short-circuits to a null `Style()` for an empty or `"none"` definition.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Style.parse returns cls.null() when the definition strips to "none" or is empty.

items.claim: `Table.add_row` validates cells at insert time rather than render time.
items.label: supported
items.reason: add_row checks is_renderable for each cell and raises errors.NotRenderableError immediately when adding the row.

items.claim: `PromptBase.check_choice()` performs an exact string membership check when case-sensitive.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When case_sensitive, check_choice returns value.strip() in self.choices, an exact membership test.

items.claim: `_check_buffer` deletes the buffer and drops output when `self.quiet` is set.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _check_buffer does `del self._buffer[:]` and returns when self.quiet is True.

items.claim: `Style.__bool__` returns `False` for a null style.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __bool__ returns `not self._null`, i.e. False for a null style.

items.claim: `Text.wrap` calls `divide_line(str(line), width, fold=True)` for each line.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: wrap calls divide_line(str(line), width, fold=wrap_overflow == "fold") and only in the non-no_wrap branch, so fold is not always True.

items.claim: `Progress.task_ids` returns IDs of all non-removed tasks.
items.label: supported
items.reason: task_ids returns list(self._tasks.keys()) and remove_task deletes entries from _tasks.

items.claim: `Table.add_row`'s `add_cell` closure appends the value to `column._cells`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The add_cell closure does column._cells.append(renderable).

items.claim: `Segment.split_and_crop_lines` at `self.width` is the only unconditional enforcement of the console width.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: In print the split_and_crop_lines call is guarded by `if crop:` while in log it is unguarded; the exclusivity claim ("the only") is too broad/vague to settle from the shown code.

items.claim: Jupyter detection checks for the presence of `get_ipython` in the global namespace.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _is_jupyter references get_ipython and returns False on NameError, then inspects the shell class.

items.claim: When recording is enabled, `Console` maintains a thread-safe buffer `_record_buffer` of rendered `Segment` objects.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Console keeps _record_buffer: List[Segment] guarded by _record_buffer_lock and extends it when record is enabled.

items.claim: The `Spinner` class uses a registry of predefined animation frames and updates based on the current time during the render cycle.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Spinner looks up frames in the SPINNERS registry and __rich_console__ renders a frame computed from console.get_time().
